subject: general
question: The ‘86th amendment of Constitution’ in December 2002 led to inserting of which fundamental right?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Education.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Right to Education was made a fundamental right by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002.
 
• 86th Constitutional Amendment Act 2002 added **Article 21 A** which declares that the state shall provide free and **compulsory education to all children of age six to fourteen years.**
 
• It has made only elementary education a fundamental right but not professional of higher education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• For its implementation Parliament passed the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act in 2009.
 
• This act is also known as the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act because of its provision of, “the fundamental right of every child between the ages of 6 to 14 with specifies minimum norms in elementary schools.
 
• The RTE Act of the Parliament of India was enacted on 4 August 2009 and came into effect from 1st April 2010. 
 
• Earlier the right was there in the constitution under article 45 in Parts IV under the directive principle of state policy.
